note: The Merovingian Franks and the Lombard Kingdom of Italy maintained generally hostile but occasionally cooperative relations throughout the 6th–8th centuries. The Merovingians periodically attempted to assert overlordship over the Lombards and intervened in Italian politics; Lombard expansion southward into central Italy was checked by Frankish-papal pressure. The Lombard-Merovingian relationship was complicated by Arian-Catholic religious differences (the Lombards were initially Arian); the conversion of the Lombard queen Theodolinda to Catholicism (c. 589) and the gradual Lombard conversion shifted the dynamic. The Lombard kingdom was ultimately conquered by Charlemagne (774) at papal request.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Merovingian-Lombard relationship establishes the pattern of Frankish intervention in Italian affairs; the Lombard threat to Rome drives the papacy's search for Frankish protection that eventually produces Charlemagne's empire; the Lombard kingdom's Catholic conversion creates the conditions for the papal-Lombard accommodation that makes it vulnerable to Frankish conquest
